## formal
\emph{Setting.} Under the representatives of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} the populated towers have space dimension $D_{r} = 3$ for this world ($r = 6$) and the mirror ($r = 2$), $D_{r} = 2$ for $r = 1, 7$ and $D_{r} = 4$ for $r = 3, 5$. A \emph{filling} gives each of them a quantum mass $m_{r} > 0$ and a number $\nu_{r} > 0$ of quanta per unit volume of its own space, in one unit of length $d$. The stored sourcing rule (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}), read with a length $\lambda d$ of the extra direction of a five-dimensional tower and with a three-dimensional tower's sheets $\mu d$ apart, gives the shares and the total
\[
f_{r} \;=\; \frac{m_{r}\nu_{r}}{m_{6}\nu_{6}} \times
\begin{cases} \lambda d & D_{r} = 4, \\ 1 & D_{r} = 3, \\ 1/(\mu d) & D_{r} = 2, \end{cases}
\qquad
T \;=\; \sum_{r \neq 6} f_{r} .
\]
Premise R1 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}) is $m_{r} = m$ for all $r$; R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}) is $\nu_{r} V_{D_{r}} d^{D_{r}} = 1$, with $V_{D}$ the volume of the unit ball $\B^{D}$; R3 (\claimref{dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-direction}) is $\lambda = \mu = 1$. Write (E), \emph{equal mass per unit ball}, for the statement that $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}}$ takes one value on all populated towers.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(One density law; proved.)} R1 and R2 together imply (E). Under (E) and R3, $f_{r} = V_{3}/V_{D_{r}}$ and $T = (11\pi + 16)/3\pi$, the total of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}; with the thicknesses free, $T = 1 + 8/3\mu + 16\lambda/3\pi$ as in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}. (E) implies neither R1 nor R2: for positive numbers $s_{r}$, not all equal, the filling $m_{r} = s_{r}m$, $\nu_{r} = 1/(s_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}})$ satisfies (E), violates R1 and R2, and has every share and the total unchanged. So every share, and the total, depends on R1 and R2 only through (E). The stored results that use R1 or R2 separately (the common mass and the cell radius in the cluster bound, R2's number density in the odd towers' population and survival) are not statements of the total.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Democracy of the total mass; proved, given the reading of the stored sphere form.)} Read a tower's mass per unit measure of its Euclidean de Sitter sphere $\Sph^{D_{r}+1}$ as its mass per unit volume of its space divided by one length common to all towers, as the stored sphere form does. Then the total mass of tower $r$ on the sphere of radius $\ell$ is a common factor times $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}\ell^{D_{r}}$, by $|\Sph^{D+1}| = 2\pi V_{D}$. Hence the democracy premise (\claimref{dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass}) is (E) with the unit of length set to the de Sitter radius, $d = \ell$, and with the thickness in the same unit it gives the same shares (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}); the shares do not depend on the unit, since $d$ cancels in $f_{r}$ under (E). Neither implies the other: the democracy premise leaves $m_{r}$ and $\nu_{r}$ separately free, and under R1 and R2 at $d \neq \ell$ the total masses are in the ratio $(\ell/d)^{D_{r}}$, unequal across dimensions. For the total, R1, R2 and the democracy premise supply one premise, (E).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The mirror's term is obtained twice; the premise sets are audited.)} At $D_{r} = 3$, (E) gives $f_{2} = 1$ with no further premise. Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(i) gives $f_{2} = 1$ from Premises P1, P2, the common ceiling coupling and the copy of content, with P4 discharged for the mirror, and without R1, R2 or R3; the first derivation has P2 and P3 in its past cone only through the census of towers, and not P1, P4 or the common ceiling coupling. So restricted to the reversal pair $\{2, 6\}$, (E) is a consequence of the population count, and it is a premise only on the four odd towers. The two derivations agree exactly on the proton-only branch; on the burning branch of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) the population count gives $f_{2} = 199/200$ (the stored $0.995$), so R1 read as equal mean mass per baryon fails there by one part in two hundred and the total is $(11\pi + 16)/3\pi - 1/200$; both values lie within one standard deviation ($0.065$) of the record's $5.364$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What still moves the total; proved.)} With (E) kept: thicknesses $(\lambda, \mu) = (2, 1)$ and $(1, 2)$ give $11/3 + 32/3\pi$ and $7/3 + 16/3\pi$, each more than five standard deviations from the record; one quantum per cube of side $2d$ in place of the unit ball, with thickness one side, gives exactly $5$, more than five standard deviations below; a three-dimensional tower read at $D_{r} = 4$ gives $7/3 + 8/\pi$. So R3, the shape of the cell in (E) and the dimensions of P3 are each used.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Count; audited on the stored dependence edges.)} Of the twenty-three postulates of the dark-matter subject, the past cone of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule} contains five: P2, P3, R1, R2, R3. The past cone of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}, which takes the mirror's term from the population count, contains seven, P1, P2, P3, P4, R1, R2 and the common ceiling coupling, and the stored total adds R3 as the choice $\lambda = \mu = 1$: eight. These eight are also the union over the stored statements of the total (the two above and the restatements \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-unit-ball-rule} and \claimref{simulations.imported-unit-ball-rule-family}). Of the other fifteen, four lie under stored results that vary the conditions of the total and under no statement of it: P5 (\claimref{synthesis.no-rule-p2-licenses-gives-the-thickness-of-r3}), H1 (\claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}), and H1, H2 and Premise U (\claimref{synthesis.bott-shifted-model-leaves-the-odd-towers-dimension-free}); the democracy premise lies under the two results on the de Sitter reading, which give other totals; the remaining ten (CPT covariance, the flag as datum, Hypothesis (S) carried to every tower, the six modelling premises of the cluster simulations and the registered asymmetry) lie under no stored result whose text contains the value $5.364$ or its closed form. By (i) to (iii) the eight reduce, for the total, to: P3 for the dimensions; (E) on the four odd towers; R3; and for the mirror's term either (E) on the reversal pair or P1, P2 and the common ceiling coupling. Two conditions of the total are stored as text and not as postulates: the costed single-ideal clause and the inference that all six towers are populated (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(vi), Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). The total remains a fit: (E) and R3 fix the two odd shares $4/3$ and $8/3\pi$ against one measured number.
\end{enumerate}

## technical
The stored total of dark to baryonic matter is a sum of shares, each the ratio of a tower's mass density, read per unit of this world's volume, to ours. A mass density is a quantum mass times a number density, so the shares see R1 (equal quantum masses) and R2 (one quantum per unit ball) only through their product: equal mass per unit ball, called (E) here. A filling in which each tower's quanta are heavier by its own factor and rarer by the same factor violates both R1 and R2 and has the same shares. The democracy premise, equal total mass on each tower's de Sitter sphere, is the same law (E) with the unit of length set to the de Sitter radius, by the identity $|\Sph^{D+1}| = 2\pi V_{D}$ and given the stored reading of the sphere form; the shares do not depend on the unit, so for the total the three postulates supply one premise, although none of them follows from the others as a statement. The mirror's share of one is obtained twice: from (E) at dimension three, and from the population count under P1, P2 and the common ceiling coupling, the two sharing only P2 and P3 among the subject's premises (in the first they enter through the census of towers). On the burning branch the second gives $0.995$, so the two disagree there by half a percent, inside the error bar. The thickness R3, the ball shape of the cell and the dimensions of P3 each move the total when changed. On the stored dependence edges, five of the subject's twenty-three postulates lie under the closed form and eight under the total with the mirror's term taken from the population count; fifteen lie under no stored statement of the total (four of them under results that vary its conditions).

## lay
The series fits the measured ratio of dark matter to ordinary matter, 5.364, with a rule built on several assumptions. This result sorts out which assumptions the number really uses. Two of them, that all hidden worlds have quanta of the same mass and that each holds one quantum per unit ball, matter for the number only through their product, the mass per unit ball; a third assumption, equal total mass in every world, is the same statement in other units, given the stored reading of it. The share of the mirror world is derived twice, by two largely separate routes that agree to within half a percent. Of the twenty-three assumptions filed under dark matter, at most eight stand under the number, and fifteen serve other results. Assuming all of this, the ratio is still fitted, not predicted: two shares are chosen and one number is matched.

## one-liner
Under the stored sourcing rule, every share of the dark-to-baryon total depends on R1 and R2 only through equal mass per unit ball (E); the democracy premise is (E) in the unit of the de Sitter radius, given the stored sphere reading; the mirror's term follows twice, from (E) or from P1, P2 and the common ceiling; five of the subject's twenty-three postulates lie under the closed form, eight under the total, and it remains a fit.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{(i).} The shares of the Setting are the sourcing rule of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} (a five-dimensional tower's density times the length of its extra direction; a sheet family's density per unit area over the spacing), divided by this world's density. Under R1 and R2, $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}} = m$ for every $r$, which is (E). Under (E) with common value $\kappa$, $m_{r}\nu_{r} = \kappa/(V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}})$, so
\[
f_{r} \;=\; \frac{V_{3}\,d^{3}}{V_{D_{r}}\,d^{D_{r}}} \times \bigl(\lambda d,\; 1,\; 1/(\mu d)\bigr)
\;=\; \frac{V_{3}}{V_{D_{r}}} \times \bigl(\lambda,\; 1,\; 1/\mu\bigr)
\]
for $D_{r} = 4, 3, 2$: the unit $d$ and the value $\kappa$ cancel. With $V_{2} = \pi$, $V_{3} = 4\pi/3$, $V_{4} = \pi^{2}/2$ the shares are $4/3\mu$, $1$, $8\lambda/3\pi$, and the sum over the mirror and the two towers of each odd dimension is $1 + 8/3\mu + 16\lambda/3\pi$, which at $\lambda = \mu = 1$ is $(11\pi + 16)/3\pi$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}; with $\lambda = \mu = c$ it is the function of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}). For the rescaled filling, $m_{r}\nu_{r} = m/(V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}})$ whatever the $s_{r}$, so (E) holds with $\kappa = m$ and each $f_{r}$ is as before, while $m_{r} = s_{r}m$ is not constant and $\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}} = 1/s_{r} \neq 1$ for some $r$. Since $f_{r}$ is a function of the products $m_{r}\nu_{r}$ alone, no share separates R1 and R2 from (E). (Check 1: two rescalings; rescaling the mass without the number density moves the total.)

\emph{(ii).} Let $\sigma_{r} = m_{r}\nu_{r}/(2\pi L)$ be the mass per unit $(D_{r}+1)$-measure, with one length $L$ for all towers (the stored sphere form reads one quantum per unit ball as one quantum per unit sphere, the factor $2\pi$ cancelling; any common $L$ serves). The total mass on the sphere of radius $\ell$ is
\[
M_{r} \;=\; \sigma_{r}\,|\Sph^{D_{r}+1}|\,\ell^{D_{r}+1} \;=\; \frac{\ell}{L}\; m_{r}\nu_{r}\,V_{D_{r}}\,\ell^{D_{r}},
\]
using $|\Sph^{D+1}| = 2\pi V_{D}$, which follows from the recursions $V_{D} = (2\pi/D)V_{D-2}$ and $|\Sph^{n}| = (2\pi/(n-1))|\Sph^{n-2}|$ with $V_{0} = 1$, $V_{1} = 2$, $|\Sph^{1}| = 2\pi$, $|\Sph^{2}| = 4\pi$ by induction on $D$. So $M_{r}$ is the same for all populated towers exactly when $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}\ell^{D_{r}}$ is, which is (E) in the unit $\ell$. By (i) the shares under (E) do not depend on the unit when the thickness is measured in it, which is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}'s agreement of the two forms. Under R1 and R2 in the unit $d$, $M_{r} = (\ell/L)\,m\,(\ell/d)^{D_{r}}$, which takes three different values on $D_{r} = 2, 3, 4$ unless $\ell = d$; and the democracy premise constrains only the products $m_{r}\nu_{r}$. (Check 2: the identity for $D = 0$ to $8$ from the two recursions; equal masses at $\ell = d$, the ratios $(\ell/d)^{D+1}$ of the check's normalisation $L = d$ otherwise.)

\emph{(iii).} At $D_{r} = 3$ the share under (E) is $V_{3}/V_{3} = 1$. Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(i) states $f_{2} = \epsilon_{2}n_{2}m_{2}/\epsilon_{6}n_{6}m_{6} = 1$ in its own notation, a ratio of mass densities in two three-dimensional spaces, which is (E) on the pair $\{2, 6\}$ whatever the unit. Its premises are those it names. That the past cone of the first derivation contains none of P1, P4 and the common ceiling coupling, and that of the second none of R1, R2 and R3, was read from the stored dependence edges (clause (v)); P2 and P3 are in both. On the burning branch Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) gives the ratio of mean masses per baryon as $0.995 = 199/200$ at equal number densities, so $m_{2} \neq m_{6}$ there and the total with that term is smaller by $1/200$. With $3.14159265358 < \pi < 3.14159265359$ both totals lie in $(5.359, 5.365)$, inside $5.364 \pm 0.065$. (Check 3.)

\emph{(iv).} Substitute in the formula of (i): $(\lambda, \mu) = (2, 1)$ gives $1 + 8/3 + 32/3\pi \approx 7.06$ and $(1, 2)$ gives $1 + 4/3 + 16/3\pi \approx 4.03$. For cubic cells of side $2d$, $m_{r}\nu_{r} = m/(2d)^{D_{r}}$, and with thickness $2d$ each odd share is $(2d)^{3}/(2d)^{D_{r}} \times (2d)^{D_{r}-3} = 1$, so $T = 5$, the stored value for cubic cells. A tower with $D_{r} = 2$ read at $D_{r} = 4$ exchanges a term $4/3$ for $8/3\pi$. (Check 4.)

\emph{(v).} The cones were computed from the built graph of the store at the pinned versions, following uses, assumes, founded\_on, specialises and derived\_from edges, and intersected with the list of entities of status postulate and subject dark-matter. The reduction is (i) to (iii). The stored statements of the total and the results that vary it were found by a pattern search of every claim's text for the value $5.364$, $5.3643$ and the closed form (thirteen entities, two of them conjectured observations and one a postulate, with empty cones); their cones are as stated in (v), the postulate-by-result lists being those of \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule} and \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness} for the eight. The fifteen postulates outside the eight are the democracy premise, P5, CPT covariance, the flag as datum, H1, H2, Hypothesis (S) carried to every tower, Premise U, the six modelling premises of the cluster simulations and the registered asymmetry.

check_py:
"""synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r2-and-d-only-as-mass-per-unit-ball: exact checks.

Numbers of Q(pi) are rational functions GA.RF in one variable standing for pi (pi is transcendental, so two such
functions are equal as reals exactly when they are equal as rational functions). Decimal comparisons use the
rational bounds PI_LO < pi < PI_HI. Ball volumes V_D come from V_0 = 1, V_1 = 2, V_D = (2 pi / D) V_(D-2); sphere
measures |S^n| from |S^0| = 2, |S^1| = 2 pi, |S^n| = (2 pi / (n-1)) |S^(n-2)|: two separate recursions.

A filling is, per populated tower, a quantum mass and a number of quanta per unit volume of the tower's own space
(space dimension D = 2, 3 or 4), in one unit of length d. The stored sourcing reads a tower's mass density per unit
of this world's three-volume through a length lam * d of each extra direction (D = 4) or with sheets mu * d apart
(D = 2); the stored premise R3 is lam = mu = 1.

(1) Shares and total from an arbitrary filling; R1 and R2 give V_3/V_D and (11 pi + 16)/(3 pi). Rescaling the mass
    of each tower by its own factor and the number density by the inverse factor breaks R1 and R2 and keeps every
    share; rescaling the mass alone moves the total.
(2) The sphere law (equal mass per unit sphere of the tower's Euclidean spacetime, dimension D + 1) gives the same
    shares, by |S^(D+1)| = 2 pi V_D from the two recursions (D = 0 to 8). The total mass of a tower on its sphere of
    radius ell, filled at one quantum per ball of radius d, is proportional to (ell/d)^(D+1): equal across the three
    dimensions only at ell = d.
(3) The mirror term: 1 from the density law at D = 3; 199/200 on the burning branch of the stored mirror share; the
    two totals differ by 1/200 and both lie within one standard deviation of the record's ratio.
(4) Each remaining premise moves the total: thickness (2, 1) and (1, 2); cubic cells of side two units give exactly
    5, more than five standard deviations below the record; a tower moved from D = 2 to D = 4 changes it.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

PI = GA.RF.var()
C = GA.RF.const
PI_LO, PI_HI = F(314159265358, 10 ** 11), F(314159265359, 10 ** 11)
OBS = F(1200, 10000) / F(2237, 100000)        # Omega_c h^2 / Omega_b h^2 of the stored comparison
SIG = F(65, 1000)
ODD_DIMS = [2, 2, 4, 4]                        # residues 1, 7, 3, 5 under the stored representatives
MIRROR_DIM = 3
OUR_DIM = 3


def ball(D):
    V = {0: C(1), 1: C(2)}
    for n in range(2, D + 1):
        V[n] = C(F(2, n)) * PI * V[n - 2]
    return V[D]


def sphere(n):
    S = {0: C(2), 1: C(2) * PI}
    for k in range(2, n + 1):
        S[k] = C(F(2, k - 1)) * PI * S[k - 2]
    return S[n]


def between(x):
    """rational lower and upper bounds of a rational function of pi that is monotone data: evaluate at both ends"""
    a, b = x.eval(PI_LO), x.eval(PI_HI)
    return min(a, b), max(a, b)


def share(D, mass, number, our_mass, our_number, lam=F(1), mu=F(1)):
    """mass density per unit of our three-volume over ours, for a tower of space dimension D"""
    rho = C(mass) * number
    if D == 4:
        rho = rho * C(lam)
    elif D == 2:
        rho = rho / C(mu)
    return rho / (C(our_mass) * our_number)


def total(filling, lam=F(1), mu=F(1)):
    """filling: dict tower -> (D, mass, number density); tower 'us' is this world"""
    _, m0, n0 = filling["us"]
    t = C(0)
    for name, (D, m, n) in filling.items():
        if name != "us":
            t = t + share(D, m, n, m0, n0, lam, mu)
    return t


def unit_ball_filling(scale=None, mass=F(1)):
    """R1 and R2: mass m, one quantum per unit ball; optional per-tower factor s: mass s m, number 1/(s V_D)"""
    towers = {"us": OUR_DIM, "mirror": MIRROR_DIM, "r1": 2, "r7": 2, "r3": 4, "r5": 4}
    out = {}
    for name, D in towers.items():
        s = F(1) if scale is None else scale[name]
        out[name] = (D, mass * s, C(1) / (C(s) * ball(D)))
    return out


CLOSED = (C(11) * PI + C(16)) / (C(3) * PI)


def check_total_depends_on_mass_times_number_only():
    premise("dark-matter.unit-ball-rule")
    premise("dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones")
    base = unit_ball_filling()
    GA.check("R1 and R2 give the stored closed form", total(base).eqrf(CLOSED))
    _, m0, n0 = base["us"]
    GA.check("share 4/3 at D = 2", share(2, *base["r1"][1:], m0, n0).eqrf(C(F(4, 3))))
    GA.check("share 8/(3 pi) at D = 4", share(4, *base["r3"][1:], m0, n0).eqrf(C(F(8, 3)) / PI))
    scales = [
        ({"us": F(1), "mirror": F(1), "r1": F(3), "r7": F(1, 5), "r3": F(7, 2), "r5": F(11)},
         C(1) + C(F(64, 15)) + C(F(116, 3)) / PI),
        ({"us": F(2), "mirror": F(5, 3), "r1": F(1, 9), "r7": F(4), "r3": F(1), "r5": F(13, 7)},
         C(F(5, 6)) + C(F(74, 27)) + C(F(80, 21)) / PI),
    ]
    for sc, mass_only in scales:
        f = unit_ball_filling(scale=sc)
        masses = {v[1] for v in f.values()}
        GA.check("the rescaled filling breaks R1", len(masses) >= 5)
        GA.check("the rescaled filling breaks R2",
                 sum(1 for k in f if not (f[k][2] * ball(f[k][0])).eqrf(C(1))) >= 4)
        GA.check("mass per unit ball is common", all((C(f[k][1]) * f[k][2] * ball(f[k][0])).eqrf(C(1)) for k in f))
        GA.check("every share is kept", total(f).eqrf(CLOSED))
        # mass rescaled without the compensating number density: the total moves, to the value computed by hand
        g = {k: (f[k][0], f[k][1], base[k][2]) for k in f}
        GA.check("mass alone moves the total", total(g).eqrf(mass_only) and not mass_only.eqrf(CLOSED))
    return True


def check_sphere_law_is_the_ball_law_and_fixes_the_unit():
    premise("dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball")
    for D in range(0, 9):
        GA.check("hat-box at D = %d" % D, sphere(D + 1).eqrf(C(2) * PI * ball(D)))
    for D in (2, 3, 4):
        GA.check("sphere share equals ball share at D = %d" % D,
                 (sphere(4) / sphere(D + 1)).eqrf(ball(3) / ball(D)))
    GA.check("sphere measures 2 pi^2, 8 pi^2/3, pi^3",
             sphere(3).eqrf(C(2) * PI * PI) and sphere(4).eqrf(C(F(8, 3)) * PI * PI)
             and sphere(5).eqrf(PI * PI * PI))

    def sphere_mass(D, ell, d):
        # one quantum of unit mass per ball of radius d, read per unit (D+1)-measure with the factor 1/(2 pi d),
        # integrated over the sphere of radius ell
        dens = C(1) / (ball(D) * C(d ** D)) / (C(2) * PI * C(d))
        return dens * sphere(D + 1) * C(ell ** (D + 1))

    for ell, d in [(F(1), F(1)), (F(7, 3), F(7, 3))]:
        ms = [sphere_mass(D, ell, d) for D in (2, 3, 4)]
        GA.check("equal total masses at ell = d", ms[0].eqrf(ms[1]) and ms[1].eqrf(ms[2]))
    for ell, d in [(F(2), F(1)), (F(1), F(3)), (F(5, 4), F(1))]:
        ms = [sphere_mass(D, ell, d) for D in (2, 3, 4)]
        r = ell / d
        GA.check("total masses in ratio (ell/d)^(D+1)",
                 ms[0].eqrf(C(r ** 3)) and ms[1].eqrf(C(r ** 4)) and ms[2].eqrf(C(r ** 5)))
        GA.check("democracy of the total mass fails at ell != d", not ms[0].eqrf(ms[1]))
        # the shares do not see the unit: the filling at radius d has the same total
    return True


def check_mirror_term_is_obtained_twice():
    premise("dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent")
    premise("dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile")
    premise("dark-matter.unit-ball-rule")
    base = unit_ball_filling()
    _, m0, n0 = base["us"]
    GA.check("the density law gives the mirror share one", share(3, *base["mirror"][1:], m0, n0).eqrf(C(1)))
    burning = F(199, 200)                       # stored mean mass per baryon ratio on the burning branch
    f = dict(base)
    f["mirror"] = (3, base["mirror"][1] * burning, base["mirror"][2])
    t_burn = total(f)
    GA.check("the two totals differ by 1/200", (CLOSED - t_burn).eqrf(C(F(1, 200))))
    for t in (CLOSED, t_burn):
        lo, hi = between(t)
        GA.check("within one standard deviation of the record", OBS - SIG < lo and hi < OBS + SIG)
    lo, hi = between(CLOSED)
    GA.check("closed form in (5.36431, 5.36433)", F(536431, 100000) < lo and hi < F(536433, 100000))
    return True


def check_each_remaining_premise_moves_the_total():
    premise("dark-matter.total-function-thickness")
    base = unit_ball_filling()
    t21 = total(base, lam=F(2), mu=F(1))
    t12 = total(base, lam=F(1), mu=F(2))
    GA.check("thickness (2, 1)", t21.eqrf(C(F(11, 3)) + C(F(32, 3)) / PI))
    GA.check("thickness (1, 2)", t12.eqrf(C(F(7, 3)) + C(F(16, 3)) / PI))
    GA.check("both differ from the closed form", not t21.eqrf(CLOSED) and not t12.eqrf(CLOSED))
    lo, hi = between(t21)
    GA.check("thickness (2, 1) is far above the record", lo > OBS + 5 * SIG)
    lo, hi = between(t12)
    GA.check("thickness (1, 2) is far below the record", hi < OBS - 5 * SIG)
    # cubic cells of side 2 (the cube circumscribing the unit ball), thickness one cell side
    towers = {"us": 3, "mirror": 3, "r1": 2, "r7": 2, "r3": 4, "r5": 4}
    cubes = {k: (D, F(1), C(F(1, 2 ** D))) for k, D in towers.items()}
    t_cube = total(cubes, lam=F(2), mu=F(2))
    GA.check("cubic cells give exactly 5", t_cube.eqrf(C(5)))
    GA.check("5 is more than five standard deviations below", F(5) < OBS - 5 * SIG)
    # one three-dimensional tower read at space dimension 4 instead of 2 (a change of representative)
    moved = dict(base)
    moved["r1"] = (4, base["r3"][1], base["r3"][2])
    t_moved = total(moved)
    GA.check("a changed representative moves the total",
             t_moved.eqrf(C(F(7, 3)) + C(8) / PI) and not t_moved.eqrf(CLOSED))
    return True
